call_points.text: No numeric FY27 guidance; management expects foreign arrivals back to normalcy in Q3 and Q4.
Kolkata Oberoi opening moved to 2029 from 2028 on heritage safety work and a city-wide construction halt.
Analyst pressed on the Kolkata delay and cost overruns; management said delays do raise costs and defer revenue.
Management declined to quantify Rajgarh's revenue contribution or management fee income.
Management declined to give revenue growth guidance for the next three to five years.
825 owned keys to be added by 2030; Trident Vizag opens 2027 through EIH Associated Hotels.
Oberoi Grand partial opening still targeted for September 2026 despite structural issues found.
Oberoi Gandikota pushed to 2030 from 2028 after a site change and redesign.
Q4 other expenses rose on airport levy from OFS, repairs, CSR, legal costs and donation.
Q4 foreign business was about 50% of the mix; domestic demand more than compensated weaker foreign bookings.
April and May were better than expected on strong domestic demand, though no numbers were given.
West Asia conflict impact on bookings not quantified; foreign travel hit but offset by domestic.
Managed-hotel delays are owner-driven and outside EIH's control; FY27 looks light on additions.
Mashobra case settled in June; hotel operations continue till October pending further development.

penalties.details: The Assistant Commissioner, Mumbai vide its order dated 31st December 2025 has levied a penalty of Rs 90,69,113/- under Section 74 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act,2017 on Trident Nariman Point and The Oberoi Mumbai, the hotels of the Company. The said penalty is mainly in relation to ITC claim on input services for the Financial Years 2018-19 to FY 2022-23.
penalties.impact: The financial impact of the aforesaid order is to the extent of the penalty imposed.

penalties.authority: The Additional Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai
penalties.details: The Additional Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai vide its review order dated 6th February 2026 has levied a penalty of Rs 29,97,50,261/- under Section 25 of the Maharashtra VAT Act, 2002 on the hotels and divisions of the Company at Mumbai. The said penalty is mainly in relation to arbitrary enhancement on Food and Beverage and other output services for the Financial Year 2016-17. Previously the company had opted for Amnesty under Settlement of arrears under the Maharashtra Settlement of Arrears of Tax, interest, penalty or Late Fee Act, 2023 for the FY 2016-17 and authorities had issued settlement order on 18.12.2023 confirming the settlement application.
penalties.impact: The financial impact of the aforesaid order is to the extent of the penalty imposed.

operating_notes.text: FY26 owned-hotel occupancy was 76.8% and RevPAR about ₹17,400, up 8.5% YoY.
Q4 owned-hotel ARR rose to ₹28,198 from ₹24,548; all-domestic ARR rose to ₹26,536 from ₹23,648.
FY26 capex of ₹680 Cr included about ₹330 Cr for Mumbai leasehold-to-freehold land conversion, ₹125 Cr on Oberoi Rajgarh and about ₹100 Cr on renovations.
Q1FY27 RevPAR across all hotels including managed rose to ₹12,801 from ₹11,352 a year ago.
OFS flight catering revenue was ₹154 Cr in Q1FY27, helped by new flights and international airlines.
Managed pipeline is 23 hotels with 1,833 keys; seven owned/associate hotels are in development.
